stem: In a Type III (Class 3) occlusion, how do the upper and lower teeth relate to each other?

options.text: The midlines of the upper and lower jaws are perfectly aligned.
The lower teeth are positioned significantly forward (protrusive).
The lower jaw is retruded, sitting far behind the upper teeth.
The upper teeth are tucked inside the lower teeth posteriorly.

explanation: A Class III bite is defined by the lower jaw protruding further forward than the upper jaw.
rationale: Consider the term 'protrusive' mentioned in the demonstration.

optionExplanations.A: Alignment of midlines is a characteristic of a standard Type I dentition.
optionExplanations.B: A Class III bite is defined by the lower jaw protruding further forward than the upper jaw.
optionExplanations.C: This describes a different malocclusion where the lower jaw is set back, rather than forward.
optionExplanations.D: Class III focuses on the anterior-posterior relationship of the jaws, primarily the forward projection of the mandible.
